sources.what: architect Karim Chakor; opened 2014; 3 storeys, 9,400 m2; white facade with colonnade of double arches in Arab-Moorish inspiration; steel and plaster frieze; central patio atrium

style.vernacular: Atlantic-coast capital of white and cream render. The Kasbah of the Udayas and medina have whitewashed, blue-trimmed houses and ochre rammed-earth ramparts; Henri Prost's 1910s-30s ville nouvelle has 4-6 storey neo-Moorish, Art Deco and modernist blocks in cream stucco with green glazed-tile roofs on public buildings; recent districts are flat-roofed concrete and render blocks.
style.ornament: Horseshoe and multifoil arches, carved sebka lozenge panels, zellij tilework in green, white and blue, green-glazed pyramidal tile roofs, studded wooden doors, crenellated ochre ramparts.

brief.name: Ramses Wissa Wassef Art Centre
brief.subject: The Wissa Wassef Art Centre at Harraniya: a cluster of low sand-coloured mud-brick studios with vaults and domes among gardens and trees

sources.what: city style only (beige concrete/brick fabric, Khedival downtown, Mamluk stonework); no building-specific description found

brief.notes: No OSM data. The vaulted mud-brick buildings in the tradition of Hassan Fathy are from general knowledge; none of the fetched pages covered it. Low.

style.vernacular: Dense sand-coloured city: 6-12 storey concrete-frame apartment blocks infilled with brick, often unrendered red brick or dusty beige render with flat roofs cluttered with water tanks, dishes and laundry; Khedival-era Haussmann-style downtown blocks in cream stone with iron balconies; Mamluk and Ottoman limestone mosques with banded stonework; modern gated compounds and malls in beige stone and glass.
style.ornament: Mashrabiya timber lattice screens and projecting balconies; muqarnas cornices and keel arches on Mamluk stonework; ablaq (alternating dark and light) banded masonry; Khedival neoclassical pediments and iron balcony rails; pharaonic revival motifs (lotus, cavetto cornice) on 1950s-60s monuments.

style.vernacular: Hot humid Indian Ocean port: German-era (1890s-1916) and British-era coral-stone and rendered colonial buildings with arched verandas, Indian-style balconies and Swahili carved doors in Kisutu, Upanga and the old centre; dense 2-6 storey painted-concrete shophouses in Kariakoo; 1960s-70s modernist government blocks; new glass-and-concrete towers and malls; houses in painted render with corrugated or rust-red metal roofs.

brief.name: Boubou Hama National Museum
brief.subject: The national museum park: a Neo-Sudanic pinnacled exhibition building with, scattered through shaded grounds, five traditional dwellings (Hausa flat-roofed banco house, Songhai/Zarma and Fulani round thatched huts, Tuareg mat hut) and a small domed shelter for the Tree of Ténéré

features.note: five traditional houses: Fulani, Hausa, Songhai, Tuareg, Zarma
Neo-Sudanic parapet pinnacles on main building
bust of Boubou Hama and giraffe sculptures

sources.what: Opened 1959 as the Musée National du Niger; museum in a park with cultural and scientific sections and a zoo; five traditional houses for Fulani, Hausa, Songhai, Tuareg, Zarma; Tree of Ténéré remains in own mausoleum since 1979; Neo-Sudanic category; bust and giraffe sculptures by Issoufou Lankondé

brief.notes: Source gives layout and the five-house programme but not facade design or colours; banco/ochre colours and pinnacles follow the Neo-Sudanic classification and local vernacular. The zoo is omitted from the model.

style.vernacular: Hot Sahelian river capital on the Niger: low (1-3 storey) flat-roofed compounds of sun-dried banco mud brick or cement-block rendered in sand, ochre or cream, behind plastered boundary walls; round thatched and conical-roofed huts and mat houses in older and rural-style quarters; wide boulevards and roundabouts; 1970s-80s uranium-era civic buildings in a Neo-Sudanic revival with pinnacled parapets; newer concrete and glass blocks in the centre.
style.ornament: Hausa-style incised and relief geometric patterns on banco facades and gateways, battlemented/pinnacled parapets and toron-like projecting beams on Neo-Sudanic civic buildings, whitewashed or ochre rendered boundary walls, round thatched Songhai/Zarma/Fulani huts and Tuareg mat dwellings at heritage sites.

sources.what: Niamey: grid plan with roundabouts, mudbrick as the common local material, uranium-funded 1970s-80s public buildings in a revival of the Sudanese style, 2010s multi-storey business districts
Niger national museum is categorised under Neo-Sudanic architecture; five traditional houses (Fulani, Hausa, Songhai, Tuareg, Zarma) are shown

brief.name: Oceanographic Museum of Monaco
brief.subject: Oceanographic Museum of Monaco: a monumental Baroque Revival palace of pale La Turbie stone clinging to the sea cliff, with a long frieze and a wide entrance stair

sources.what: About 100,000 tons of La Turbie stone, 85 m high (from sea level), frieze with names of twenty research vessels, Baroque Revival, set into sea cliff, inaugurated 1910 after eleven years

brief.notes: Height 85 m is measured from the sea-level foot of the cliff; the building above the street is about 40 m. Present the street-side facade and the long sea-edge frieze. White/cream limestone, no bright colours.

style.vernacular: A dense hillside city-state on the Riviera: Belle Epoque and Beaux-Arts buildings in cream limestone and warm ochre, apricot, pink and pale yellow render with stucco ornament, wrought-iron balconies and green shutters; the Rock of Monaco-Ville has medieval Genoese-Italian houses in pastel render and a Louis XIV-style palace; modern Fontvieille is reclaimed land with white and cream mid-rise blocks with terraces and balconies; high-rises and glass towers climb the slopes. Mansard roofs in zinc or slate, terracotta tile, copper cupolas with green patina; palms, pines, agave and bougainvillea.
style.ornament: Garnier-era Beaux-Arts: carved pediments, caryatids, balustrades, twin ornate towers, wrought-iron balconies, striped awnings; Genoese pastel render with shutters and trompe-l oeil window frames on the Rock; Baroque Revival cliff-front staircases; terraces and balconies throughout.

sources.what: French Belle Epoque with Italian/Genoese influence, Louis XIV palace, cream-coloured stone cathedral, locally sourced granite, marble and terracotta tile in modern buildings, coloured turrets, terraces and balconies. Specific hex colours are from general photographic knowledge of Monaco rather than a citation.
